correctness.rationale: For L_n=P_n □ P_2 a forbidden monochromatic triple lies on a shortest path of ≤5 edges. On L_5, every opposite-corner shortest path has six vertices; any three-coloring would use each color exactly twice. Comparing consecutive vertical-crossing positions gives t_(j+1)=b_j and b_(j+1)=t_j for j=0..3, hence t_0=t_2=t_4, a forbidden threefold color on the 4-edge top-row geodesic. The period-four column pairs (0,1),(1,0),(2,3),(3,2) cannot create any triple on ≤5-edge geodesics: each row has four distinct consecutive colors; crossing paths with h≤3 horizontal steps have at most one occurrence per row; for h=4 interior crosses have ≤4 in each portion, while endpoint crosses have a singleton different from the repeated endpoint color. Short ladders have chromatic minima 1,2,2,3 for n=1..4; n=4 witness (0,0),(1,2),(2,1),(1,2). Thus n≥5 and both infinite ladders equal 4. Independent exhaustive forbidden-triple backtracking for n=1..5 reproduced [1,2,2,3,4]. The argument, not this finite census, proves all n.

originality.rationale: Cody–Detore define the exact metric general-position parameter and explicitly pose ladder grids in Question 6.2; their path/cycle formulas do not answer the width-two family. Chandran et al. establish the unrestricted GP chromatic number of width-two ladders, which covers some short cases but grows with n; it cannot imply the fixed five-edge coloring=4 for all n≥7. Cody–Moore thin-grid maximum (3,d)-independent-set counts do not in general force a partition into minimum color classes. Best-of-knowledge original for the unbounded ladder family.

value.rationale: A complete sharp fixed-distance coloring formula resolves a specifically posed family of Cartesian-product-of-paths examples. It separates local bounded geodesic coloring from unrestricted general-position coloring for arbitrarily long grids, starting at n=7; a minimum-color explicit periodic pattern and minimal five-column obstruction are reusable structural information.

limitations: Exact only for geodesic length at most five, monochromatic multiplicity at most two, width two; no taller Cartesian-grid formula.
